claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 rapidly quenched at rates above 10^5 K/s has an incompletely amorphous structure.
The rapidly quenched alloy exhibits extensive primary non-eutectic crystallization.
The alloy undergoes a multistep crystallization sequence during reheating.
The proposed intervention is a flash reheating pulse applied immediately after rapid quenching.
The flash pulse should heat the alloy at approximately 10^3 K/s to a temperature above Tg but below Tx for a few seconds.
Subsequent thermal analysis should use a DSC reheating rate of approximately 10 K/min.
A flash pulse between Tg and Tx will dissolve incipient crystalline nuclei formed during quenching.
The pulse will revert embryonic crystallites to a disordered state.
The pulse will inhibit subsequent growth of primary non-eutectic phases.
Flash reheating supplies enough energy to melt very small crystalline nuclei without allowing substantial nucleation or growth.
Eliminating the nuclei resets the crystallization process and stabilizes the amorphous matrix.
The flash treatment will postpone crystallization during subsequent reheating.
Flash-treated samples will have a greater amorphous phase fraction than untreated rapidly quenched samples.
Flash-treated samples will show reduced exothermic crystallization peaks in DSC.
Flash-treated samples will show a higher DSC crystallization-onset temperature than untreated samples.
Pulse temperatures or durations outside the proposed thermal window may either fail to dissolve nuclei or induce additional crystallization.
